comparisons.peer_summary: As of November 3, 2024, the company's primary liquidity sources included $9,348 million in cash and cash equivalents, expected operating cash flows, and $7.5 billion in available capacity under its unsecured revolving credit facility.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose their primary cash and cash equivalent balances as a key component of liquidity. AMD reported $5.1 billion as of December 28, 2024, down from $5.8 billion in the prior year, while AVGO reported $9,348 million (approximately $9.3 billion) as of November 3, 2024, down from $14,189 million in the prior year. While AMD focuses the narrative on the balance reduction and domestic hold percentage, AVGO includes expected operating cash flows and revolving credit capacity in its primary liquidity definition.

sentences.text: As of December 28, 2024, our cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $5.1 billion compared to $5.8 billion as of December 30, 2023.

Our primary sources of liquidity as of November 3, 2024 consisted of: (i) $9,348 million in cash and cash equivalents, (ii) cash we expect to generate from operations and (iii) available capacity under our $7.5 billion unsecured revolving credit facility.

comparisons.peer_topic: Repatriation of non-U.S. cash and tax implications
comparisons.peer_summary: Substantially all non-U.S. cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities are available for use in the U.S. without additional federal income taxes, except for approximately $1.4 billion for which no related foreign or state taxes have been accrued if repatriated.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the geographic allocation and repatriation status of their non-U.S. cash holdings. AMD specifies that 90% of its cash and cash equivalents were held domestically as of December 28, 2024, up from 77% previously. NVDA states that substantially all cash held outside the U.S. is available for use in the U.S. without additional federal income taxes, except for approximately $1.4 billion. Both items address the management and tax implications of cross-border cash positions.

sentences.text: The percentage of cash and cash equivalents held domestically was 90% as of December 28, 2024, and 77% as of December 30, 2023.

Except for approximately $1.4 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities held outside the U.S. for which we have not accrued any related foreign or state taxes if we repatriate these amounts to the U.S., substantially all of our cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities held outside of the U.S. at the end of fiscal year 2024 are available for use in the U.S. without incurring additional U.S. federal income taxes.
